caseIdentity.comparison: Literal source names fetched at the immutable commit exactly match the 51 unique TAP subtests and their numbered ok lines; Node reports files in the observed order, which differs from command argument order.

lost real COMMIT acknowledgments never reacquire reservations or duplicate committed revisions
a restarted compute adapter reconciles a lost allocation acknowledgment without a second POST

action success and exact powered-off observation are both required after asynchronous creation

missing ambiguous or paginated lost-ack recovery cannot allocate another server
foreign dependencies and withdrawn fresh admission fail before provider mutation
every existing-target owner label and stored ID is checked before power or deletion

graceful shutdown is explicit and never silently forces poweroff
deletion needs absent exact resource and terminal action while retaining external resource limits

provider rejection rate limits malformed bodies and server failures remain bounded redacted outcomes

backward clocks missing operations and mismatched server topology stay fenced without writes

logs.hashEncoding: SHA-256 of exact connector-decoded log text encoded UTF-8, including the leading BOM; no raw logs or registry bearer token retained.

tap.encoding: Timestamp-prefix-stripped TAP section from TAP version 13 through duration_ms, with one terminal newline; diagnostic body retained in this digest, not persisted as another artifact.

registry.jsonLineEncoding: Exact compact JSON output line, no timestamp prefix or terminal newline.

meaningfulPostgresScope: Real PostgreSQL clients compete for one durable first reservation and one CAS winner.
Current receipt and append-only event commit atomically; a real event-trigger failure rolls both back.
A wrapper executes real COMMIT then drops its acknowledgement; restart/replay recovers the committed reservation/revision without duplicate events.
Established server/action IDs, operation/request uniqueness and exact binding/fence/hash remain fenced.
Real role/forced-RLS and least-grant cases deny BFF/browser journal access and deny runtime credentials Auth-envelope/session access or workspace mutation.
An injected fake Hetzner transport loses a create acknowledgement; a restarted adapter uses the real journal and owned GET recovery without a second POST.
limits: All 51 passing cases are this immutable CI scope, separate from earlier local or backend/UI checks.
PostgreSQL was a fresh authored CI service with an auth.users stub, not Supabase or customer data; this does not prove live database/auth/session setup or production organization isolation.
Compute transport and artifact verifier were authored fakes; no live Hetzner allocation, paid resource, model, Notion call or serving Gateway was exercised.
The separate registry job performed seven anonymous pull-only metadata requests. No layers were downloaded or image installed/executed.

Digest and OCI source/version/non-root metadata linkage do not authenticate publisher provenance or prove signature, schema/protocol, sandbox, backup/restore or runtime readiness. Registry artifactAdmitted remains false.
This receipt records CI outcome and retrieved metadata; it does not apply SQL, bind worker/provider credentials, approve spend, activate dispatch/chat or prove full managed-service completion.
